fallos_mitigaciones: Substitution failure: the system infers a plausible value when evidence is missing, and 'guessed values...become seeds for downstream memory corruption' (Sec.2.1); compounding loss across summarisation/embedding compression (Sec.1.2, Sec.5.2 'Compounding loss and memory corruption'). Mitigated by schema-enforced explicit-unknown fields (values 'must never be inferred'), staged validation gates with local retries at object/field/value detection stages (Sec.6.1), and an LLM judge-in-the-loop that raises object-level accuracy from 86.61% to 90.42% and output accuracy from 50.00% to 62.67% (Table6-7).

fallos_mitigaciones: Existing graph-based memory systems suffer heavy, redundant, entangled graph structures causing slow update/inference, e.g. 'GraphRAG requires up to 20 minutes for graph and community construction per dialogue and over 2 minutes of query latency' (Sec.1); also flat/unguided retrieval returns fragmented or contextually inconsistent information (Sec.1). Mitigated by CogniGraph's lightweight hierarchical indexing (topology as scaffold, not a content repository, Sec.3.1) enabling real-time incremental updates without full re-indexing, and by a Weibull-based temporal decay function w(delta_tau) that penalizes outdated triples while retaining long-tailed relevance for distant timestamps (Sec.3.2), addressing memory staleness.

fallos_mitigaciones: Fragment-based memory retrieves isolated records without integration: the running example shows a system recalling a stale IPA preference and recommending alcohol despite a newly introduced antibiotics constraint from a later session, i.e. a failure to detect conflicts/update state (Fig.2, Sec.1). Mitigated by Semantic Consolidation, which clusters MemCells into MemScenes and maintains a compact user profile with 'recency-aware updates and conflict tracking' (Sec.3.4, Appendix B.3), plus Foresight signals with validity intervals [tstart,tend] that are filtered by current time and discarded once expired (Sec.3.3, Sec.3.5), preventing stale time-bound facts from being surfaced.

fallos_mitigaciones: Flat, monolithic memory stores entangle temporal/causal/entity information, limiting interpretability and causing 'suboptimal reasoning accuracy'; prior methods 'can retrieve what occurred but struggle to reason about why' due to missing explicit causal structure (Sec.1-2). Also addresses the 'object permanence problem' (losing track of the same entity across disjoint timeline segments) via an explicit Entity Graph (Sec.3.2). Mitigated by decoupling four orthogonal relation graphs (semantic/temporal/causal/entity) plus a dual-stream write pipeline that separates latency-sensitive ingestion from asynchronous LLM-based structural consolidation (Sec.3.4), preserving responsiveness while deepening relational structure.

fallos_mitigaciones: Semantic misalignment: extracted memories detached from original dialogue context cause errors resolving temporal references, coreference, and implicit semantics (Sec.1); memory updates in prior systems are 'typically static or similarity-driven, lacking principled mechanisms to revise or correct stored knowledge' when new info overlaps/extends/contradicts existing memory, degrading long-term consistency (Sec.1). Mitigated by the Knowledge Alignment module (temporal alignment + coreference resolution, Sec.2.2.3) -- disabling it drops Note Memory average GPT-Score from 63.44 to 57.51 (Table3) -- and by conflict-aware Memory Reconsolidation classifying new evidence as independent/extendable/contradictory and applying typed ADD/UPDATE/DELETE operations (Sec.2.4), which improves Note Memory GPT-Score by ~5.85% and overall performance by ~0.28% when enabled (Sec.4.4, Table4).

benchmarks: FHIR-AgentEval (custom sandbox, 43 tasks: appointment management + genetic testing workflows)
fallos_mitigaciones: Dominant failure modes in FHIR agent execution: incorrect tool selection (missing required tools), incorrect tool order, incorrect resource-type confusion, prohibited tool use, and raw tool errors (Sec.Error analysis, Fig.7-8); baseline and baseline+specs configurations show the highest counts for incorrect tool selection and incorrect resource type. Mitigated by Reflexion-inspired long-term memory: 'the primary benefit of long-term memory lies in reducing strategic execution errors -- such as incorrect tool or resource-type selection -- rather than isolated low-level tool mistakes' (Discussion); the best memory configuration improves held-out task success by 9.1% over baseline (Abstract), and by 22.5%/27.9% in Experiments 1/2 (Results). Runtime access to FHIR specs alone mitigates only low-level errors, not the higher-level strategic failure modes.
cita: Mokssit, Ravi, Nie, Kim & Liu (2026). FHIR-AgentEval: A Modular Sandbox for Benchmarking Clinical LLM Agents with an Evaluation of Memory-Augmented Configurations.
notes: mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL: Reflexion-inspired long-term memory stores 'micro reflections: tips about a (FHIR resource, operation) pair' and 'macro reflections: higher-level strategic planning for the task' (Sec.MCP servers) -- reusable how-to/procedural lessons for tool use, not episodic conversation or general facts. representacion=VECTOR (macro reflections embedded and retrieved via semantic similarity) + DOCS-ARCHIVOS (micro reflections stored with structured (resource,operation) metadata) -- 'dual FAISS-based memory store' (Sec.Reflexion training process). operaciones=WRITE (reflections generated and stored during offline training) + CONSOLIDACION (a reflector LLM 'turns the feedback, execution traces, and deterministic validator outcomes into reusable lessons', Sec.Reflexion training process -- a distillation/consolidation step); no runtime forgetting/update observed (memory is trained once offline and reused read-only at evaluation). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM (a reflector LLM, GPT-o4-mini, decides what lessons to extract from each training run) + EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (the reflexion pipeline fires deterministically 'after each run', Sec.Reflexion training process). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS (macro reflections retrieved via semantic similarity) + GREP-ARCHIVOS (micro reflections retrieved via exact structured (FHIR resource, operation) metadata matching -- closest available token for exact/non-fuzzy matching, not literal text grep). mide_lectura=SI: the paper's central ablation directly measures whether reading from memory improves task success across 5 configurations x 4 experimental settings (Table1, Fig.5a-b). alcance=TAREA: reflections are (resource,operation)-scoped or task-strategy-scoped lessons reused 'across tasks and variations' within the FHIR-workflow domain (Sec.Reflexion training process) -- not session/dialogue-based; TAREA is the closest fit though reuse spans multiple task instances/variations. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'the reflector can optionally query the FHIR R4 specifications MCP server to ensure reflections adhere to the standard' (Sec.MCP servers) -- specs-grounding of memory content against an authoritative source is the paper's core independent variable ('specs-trained' vs 'no-specs' memory). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;FIDELIDAD (F_screening) confirmed + COSTO added (Fig.10-12 dedicated token-usage analysis) + PROCEDIMENTAL added (the memory content itself is procedural tool-use/strategy knowledge, matching this F-facet directly) -- both additions noted per protocol. handoff=CONTENIDO: reflection lessons persist from the offline training phase and are retrieved as content across many later, independent task/agent runs. plan_estado=NO: macro reflections are procedural ADVICE about how to plan/sequence tools (a lesson/strategy), not a record of a specific task's live plan/progress state -- coded as PROCEDIMENTAL rather than plan_estado. evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (explicit: 'We run an ablation study of five agent configurations' varying specs/memory access, Table1) + BENCHMARK-E2E (43-task sandbox success rates across 4 experiments) + MEDICION-COSTO (Fig.10-12 token-usage distributions and coefficient-of-variation analysis). Key numbers: best memory config +9.1% success on held-out tasks (Abstract); +22.5% (Exp.1) and +27.9% (Exp.2) over baseline (Results); memory-enhanced configs show lower total outcome variance (2503-2643 vs 2879-2905 pct-pts squared, Fig.6b) but higher median token usage (Fig.10).
